blocks.content: Run against a container instead of an image, docker inspect returns the full runtime state: its current status, its network settings, its mounted volumes, everything Docker knows about that specific running instance.

Where inspecting an image tells you how it was built, inspecting a container tells you what is actually happening right now: whether it is running, its exit code if it stopped, and exactly when it started.

blocks.alt: The live State block is unique to inspecting a container

docker inspect web
# Includes a "State" section with Status, Running,
# ExitCode, StartedAt, and FinishedAt.

blocks.content: Beyond state, the most useful sections are NetworkSettings (the container's internal IP address and network details) and Mounts (exactly which volumes or bind mounts are attached, and where).

blocks.content: 3. A Real Use Case: Finding a Container's IP
blocks.text: 3. A Real Use Case: Finding a Container's IP

blocks.content: A very common need is finding the internal IP address Docker assigned a container, useful when debugging container-to-container networking directly. docker inspect, filtered down to the right field, answers this in one line.

blocks.alt: A one-line answer to "what is this container's IP"

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Inspecting a container returns its live runtime state, not just build-time configuration, status, IP address, and mounted volumes included.
--format lets you pull out exactly the one field you need instead of reading the entire JSON output by hand.
